title: A Figure in Open Space
question: What does the space around a figure do to it?
introduction: Eight works place figures — human, animal, skeletal, snail — inside fields that dissolve, dwarf, or press against them. Some figures lose their edges to overlapping washes; others hold a hard silhouette against a single open color. Moving through the gallery, notice how the surrounding ground shifts from active to empty, from glowing to dark.
closing: Each work leaves a different amount of room around its figure. Whether that room reads as exposure, weight, or release depends on what the figure's own edges are doing.

title: Shape, Mark, Signal
question: How much does a solid shape need before it starts to speak?
introduction: Fifteen works share a common strategy: a dark silhouette, a flat field of color, and a small number of marks that do the work of expression. This exhibition follows that strategy from its most stripped-down form to its most layered, asking at each stop what the marks add — and what the silence of the shape withholds.
closing: Each work returns to the same wager: a sealed form, a few marks, a flat field. Whether that is enough — and enough for what — the shapes leave open.

title: The Body Makes a Gesture
question: Where does movement begin in a still drawing?
introduction: Twenty-seven drawings, each built around a body caught mid-action: leaning, lunging, bowing, spreading wide, or folding inward. None of these figures are at rest, yet none are photographs of motion. The gallery asks you to track how line, weight, and the space around a form can make stillness feel like a held breath rather than a stopped clock.
closing: Each drawing fixes a body at one instant. Whether that instant reads as arrival, departure, or suspension depends on which line you follow first — and the drawings offer no single answer.

stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #32

stops.whyHere: Splayed limbs radiate in all directions; dense overlapping loops build the body and the squared, open-toothed face amplifies the sense of outward force to its loudest point in the chapter.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W122's transparency gives way to dense tangled loops, and the open mouth shifts from a lunge into something closer to a shout.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #47

stops.transitionFromPrevious: The all-directions explosion of W249 narrows here to a single diagonal pull between two unequal arms, making the imbalance more precise and quieter.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #18

stops.transitionFromPrevious: W161's asymmetric figure gives way to a composition without a readable body: the arching curve and crowded verticals carry the chapter's tension between expansion and compression in abstract form.

stops.transitionFromPrevious: W013's rigid outline gives way to warm color and a grinning face, but the spread-arm, feet-planted stance is identical, shifting tone without changing posture.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #30

stops.transitionFromPrevious: W050's warm amber ground is replaced by a yellow-green field split by a hard black diagonal, sharpening the sense that the figure is about to cross a threshold.

chapters.title: Structure Exposed: When the Body Shows Its Frame
chapters.introduction: Four figures in which the skeleton, the outline, or the interior construction becomes the subject — bodies that are simultaneously solid and see-through.

stops.whyHere: Arms spread, ribcage lines in pink and red visible through the torso, a radiating tutu shape at the waist — the figure displays its own construction as part of the pose.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W068's fraying edge gives way to a figure that makes its internal structure the central visible fact: ribs, joints, and skirt-spokes all equally exposed on a quiet olive ground.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #17

stops.whyHere: An inverted skeletal form descends through horizontal bands, bones loosely drawn with gaps between outline and fill — the structure is visible but incomplete, suspended rather than solid.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: W289's upright skeletal figure tips upside-down here, and the quiet olive ground becomes a saturated red field crossed by dark horizontal bands that read as both shadow and barrier.

title: Figures in Company
question: When do separate figures begin to form a group?
introduction: Twenty-three works line this gallery, each placing two or more figures in the same space. The question is not whether they belong together but how the visible evidence — gap, overlap, shared mark, mirrored posture — tips a collection of bodies toward something that reads as a group. Follow the progression and decide for yourself where that threshold falls.
closing: The works offer no single answer: proximity, shared marks, and overlapping outlines each make a different claim. The threshold between separate and together remains open.

title: Finding Faces in a Crowd
question: What lets one face emerge from a crowded drawing?
introduction: These twenty drawings share a single problem: too many marks, too many forms, too many possible faces. Some works announce their figures immediately; others bury them under crossing lines and competing shapes. Moving through the gallery, notice what draws your eye to one face over another — outline, color, scale, or simply the gap between two marks.
closing: Each drawing offers a different answer to the same question. Whether a face emerges depends on what the drawing withholds as much as what it shows.

chapters.title: One Face, Clearly There
chapters.introduction: These works open the gallery with figures that hold their ground — readable faces that give the eye a place to land before the crowding begins.

stops.whyHere: Black silhouettes press upward against a flat yellow field; their shared XX marks make each head legible while the group reads as a single mass.

chapters.title: The Crowd Turns Loud

stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #14

chapters.title: Figures Crossing, Lines Taking Over

stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's figures were pressed flat by color; here a black sky and spatial separation suggest depth, yet the figures still compete rather than recede.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #254

stops.whyHere: A dark mass holds center against an orange field while blue slashes cut across at angles; the white bar cluster reads as both noise and anchor in a composition that refuses to settle.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work distributed figures across a legible space; here the central form is ambiguous — mass rather than figure — and crossing diagonals deny any stable reading.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #238

stops.whyHere: Several toothy heads overlap with raised limb-like forms; broad cyan passages open brief gaps, but one face's outline keeps becoming part of another's body.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's ambiguity came from a single dominant mass; here multiple heads compete, and the cyan gaps are the only breathing room in the tangle.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #1

stops.whyHere: Heads and limb-like forms weave together in colored marks; the drawing alternates between recognizable characters and almost illegible crossings, making looking a repeated act of finding and losing.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works share overlapping heads and cyan passages, but here the colored marks layer more completely over the figures, making each face harder to hold.

stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work still offered recognizable heads amid the crossings; here the marks no longer assemble into a face — the question the gallery opened with goes unanswered.

title: What Makes a Shape a Character?
question: At what point does a shape become a character — and what tips it over that edge?
introduction: Twenty-six works line this gallery, ranging from figures whose species reads at a glance to forms where a face is barely implied. Each stop asks you to notice the specific marks — an eye shape, a posture, a mouth line — that trigger recognition. The journey moves from clear silhouettes toward ambiguity and back, testing where character begins and ends.
closing: The works offer no single answer: a spiral, a bared tooth, a crossed eye, a shadow — any one of these can be enough. The threshold keeps shifting.

title: Ground, Light, Surround
question: When does the surrounding space become part of the subject?
introduction: Sixteen works move between open landscape and enclosed figure, between cast light and dense mark. None of them lets the background stay neutral. A building dissolves into its field; a face is pressed by radiance from outside; a valley carries as much visual weight as any portrait. This exhibition traces the ways surrounding space can redirect, contain, or charge what sits inside it.
closing: Each work leaves the boundary between subject and surround unsettled. Whether that pressure comes from light, ground, or enclosure stays an open question across every room.

title: Letters Among the Marks
question: How does a readable sign change the way we look?
introduction: Across these fourteen works, words and symbols appear on the same surface as faces, figures, and dense mark-making. Sometimes a word names what we see; sometimes it sits inside a body or floats as pure shape. This exhibition traces what happens at that boundary — where reading and looking pull in different directions, and neither fully wins.
closing: Each work places a legible sign or symbol-like mark inside a field that resists easy reading. Whether that tension resolves or simply holds is a question each visitor answers differently.

title: Lines Moving Outward
question: When marks spread away from a figure, what do they carry with them?
introduction: Seventeen works share one structural habit: lines, waves, zigzags, or spikes move outward from a central form. The mood traveling with those marks shifts constantly — from stillness to noise, from containment to release. Four chapters follow that spread, asking what changes when the radiating mark is tight or loose, orderly or frantic, and when the center itself begins to dissolve.
closing: Each work sends marks outward from something. Whether those marks read as pressure, heat, noise, or escape depends on what the center looks like — and how much of it remains.

title: Across the Surface
question: When repeated marks divide a surface, what do they hold together — and what do they hold apart?
introduction: Twenty-four works share a single persistent habit: the repeated mark. Bands slice, zigzags border, grids map, spirals coil, and rows of identical units march across fields of every color. Some surfaces carry recognizable faces; others resist any figure at all. Moving through the gallery, watch how the same devices — the stripe, the zigzag, the grid — can contain a form, fracture it, or replace it entirely.
closing: Each work returns to the same question from a different angle: when a surface is divided by repeated marks, the boundary between structure and noise, between holding together and breaking apart, stays genuinely open.

title: Looking into Circles
question: When does a coiled line become an eye, and when does it stay a mark?
introduction: Thirty works share a recurring form: the spiral, the socket, the ring. Some arrange these into faces that hold a gaze. Others scatter them across the surface until the eye dissolves into pattern. Moving through these rooms, the boundary between a circle that watches and a circle that simply repeats proves less fixed than it first appears.
closing: Each room tested the same form — coil, ring, socket — against a different context. Whether any given circle reads as a gaze or a pattern may depend less on the mark itself than on what surrounds it.

title: Two Sides of a Face
question: How does a face hold together when its two sides differ?
introduction: Every face here is split: one eye open, one crossed out; one socket a spiral, one a flat disc; one cheek warm, one cold. These thirty works arrange themselves around that basic asymmetry, moving from faces where the difference is a single sharp mark to ones where the two halves seem built from entirely separate systems. Look at what holds them together — and what does not.
closing: Each face here stays in one piece despite the visible pull between its two sides. Whether that tension reads as unease, alertness, or something else remains open.

title: The Shape of a Mouth
question: When teeth appear in so many different constructions, what keeps an expression from settling into one feeling?
introduction: Twenty-three heads, each built around an open mouth. Some bare teeth in tight rows, others spread them wide across a dark void; some surround them with spirals and zigzags, others with flat color or scribbled lines. Moving through the gallery, the same raw material — white marks against a dark gap — keeps shifting between a grin, a grimace, a shout, and something that refuses all three.
closing: The tooth row reappears in every room, drawn differently each time. Whether any single construction resolves into an expression is a question the works leave open.

title: Marks Against Dark
question: Which marks let a face become visible against a dark ground?
introduction: Fifteen works share one condition: a dark field that could absorb any form placed against it. Some faces push forward through thick outline; others dissolve into the ground they occupy. Moving through the gallery, you can watch the marks that hold a face together—line, color band, crossed circle, bare tooth—and the moments when those marks stop being enough.
closing: Each work returns to the same problem: a dark ground and a set of marks trying to hold a face in place. Whether they succeed, or only partly manage it, is a question each image leaves open.

chapters.introduction: Four works where X-marks, mismatched eyes, or a split-face division are the visible device that gives the face its character against the dark.

stops.whyHere: Two red X marks over the eye sockets are the sharpest contrast against the gold skull; they simultaneously locate the eyes and block them.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's central glow radiates outward from the eye zone; here red X marks occupy the same zone and close it off, swapping emission for cancellation.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #69

stops.whyHere: One eye carries a red X-crossed circle, the other a blue iris and dark pupil; the asymmetry between sealed and open makes the face feel off-balance in a way identical marks could not.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's two X marks treat both eyes identically; here the treatment splits—one eye crossed, one open—so the face holds two different states at once.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #252

stops.whyHere: A dark vertical line divides the face: warm amber-red on one side, cool blue-grey on the other; the split is the primary mark that makes the face visible as a face.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The asymmetry above is between two eye treatments; here the whole face is divided by a single vertical line, extending the split from one feature to the entire surface.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #283

stops.whyHere: The dark-green mass would be nearly formless without the two small ringed circles near the upper center; those circles are the only marks that propose a face inside the dense crossing lines.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous face is split but fully present; here a face is barely proposed—two ringed circles in a dense field are the only evidence a head is there at all.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #23

chapters.title: Surfaces That Enclose
chapters.introduction: Three works where the face is held inside a curved or hooded form, and the question is how much of the face that enclosure actually reveals.

stops.whyHere: The rounded helmet-visor form encloses two asymmetric eyes and a gridded mouth; pale washes and a bright highlight suggest a reflective surface that shows a face without fully exposing it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous face is barely legible inside dense marks; here a rounded enclosure with a bright highlight offers more structure, yet the face inside remains incomplete and asymmetric.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #104

stops.whyHere: A large face fills the frame but colored loops spill past the jaw into the black surround, so the enclosure the head should provide keeps leaking outward.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The helmet above holds its contents; here the face has no such shell, and its marks overflow into the surrounding dark, dissolving the boundary the helmet maintained.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #134

stops.whyHere: The yellow hood is the most solid enclosure in the gallery, yet the face inside it is the darkest void—red slashes and bared teeth are all that remain where a face should be.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous face leaks outward into darkness; here the enclosure is intact and opaque, but the darkness is now inside, behind the hood.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #38

chapters.title: When the Ground Wins
chapters.introduction: Two works where the dark field or a loud surround overwhelms the face, leaving marks that suggest a head without fully delivering one—or abandoning the face entirely.

stops.whyHere: An amber ground, crossing blue bands, and scattered black masses offer no stable face; the looping lines and dots read as noise rather than features, the gallery's most dissolved image.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous hood contains darkness within a legible figure; here figure dissolves entirely—the amber field and black masses offer no face to locate.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #127

scope: Selected owned artworks; editorial exhibition, not an artist-declared grouping

findings: W300 was omitted from the draft entirely; it is now placed as the gallery's closing stop in a dedicated final chapter, grounded in its visible grey ground, hollow eye socket, open hatched lower gap, and multicolour patches beneath black scaffolding.

W282 observations describe a cat-like head with pointed peaks and four framed panels; the image confirms this. The draft's transition from W120 to W282 ('loose overlapping lines give way to a strictly gridded face') is visually supportable and retained with minor wording tightening.

W079 was placed last in Chapter 4 as a deliberate contrast to the display-board works; this is an honest contrasting role grounded in its visible gold mass, dark cavity, and absence of rectangular panels, and is retained.

W120 observations describe a large rounded form with overlapping lines and a split composition; the image confirms a loosely outlined rounded form with dense line-work at centre and a quieter right side. The role and transitions are supportable.

W193 observations describe a plated gold figure with zigzag marks and radiating background; the larger anchor image confirms this clearly. The description 'cast rather than drawn' is a metaphor not a claim about process — revised to 'solidly bounded' to stay concrete.
W110 observations describe a standing figure with a wide rectangular head, striped torso, and wandering yellow and red line loops; the image confirms this. Role and transitions are supportable.

W257 observations describe a squat figure with cyan-rimmed rectangular eye forms and a raised hand; the image confirms warm amber bulk, rectangular eye outlines, and a raised right hand. Transitions are supportable.

W094 observations describe a cat-eared head on a saturated blue field with zigzag bands and outward-pushing red strokes; the image confirms this. Transition from W257 (full crouching figure to cropped head) is a visible structural contrast and is retained.

W192 observations describe a black-ground face with rectangular blocks, mismatched eyes, and arcing coloured lines crossing the figure; the image confirms this. Transition noting lines cross directly over the face (vs W094's outward push) is visually grounded.

W082 observations describe a frontal face built from amber and rust lines with pale scribbled eye boxes and a white tooth grid; the image confirms this. Transition from W192 is grounded in the shift from multicolour crossing lines to a warmer, denser accumulation.
W032 anchor image confirms two nested square eye zones, a lower tooth rectangle, red and black field, and scattered loose lines — all observations are supportable. Opening role is retained.

W226 observations describe an olive-green field with stacked rectangular panels and mismatched spiral eyes; the image confirms this. Transition from W032 is grounded in the shared compartment logic and the visible temperature shift from red to olive.

W247 observations describe stacked nested frames, spiraling eye loops, bared teeth, and an orange field; the image confirms this. Transition from W226 is grounded in the multiplication of nested outlines and the contrast between olive and orange fields.

W263 observations describe a diamond-shaped head, wide-brimmed hat, yellow outline compartments, and soft pooling colour fields; the image confirms this. Transition from W282 is grounded in the shift from symmetrical four-panel grid to asymmetric diamond-and-hat geometry.

The phrase 'cast rather than drawn' in the W193 transition was an unsupported process claim; corrected to describe visible surface qualities only.

Chapter 4 ('Faces as Display Boards') previously ended with W079 as a contrast stop before the gallery closed; W300 is now placed in a new fifth chapter as the closing work, giving the gallery a concrete conclusion grounded in W300's visible features (grey ground, hollow socket, hatched open mouth, colour patches beneath black outlines). W079 is moved to close Chapter 4 as originally drafted, retaining its honest contrasting role.

title: Building the Head
question: What gives a drawn head its structure?
introduction: Fifteen works ask the same question through different means: rectangles stacked like brickwork, spirals coiled inside eye sockets, loose lines that escape their outlines, and colour patches sitting beneath scaffolding rather than filling it. Move through five chapters and watch how each work decides where solidity ends and pressure begins.
closing: Each work answers differently — through locked panels, escaping lines, or a hollow where a feature should be. The question of what holds a head together stays open.

chapters.title: Flat Fields and Nested Frames
chapters.introduction: These works build their faces from zones of flat colour and nested rectangles, treating the head as a system of contained compartments rather than a rounded form.

stops.whyHere: A red-and-black field holds two nested square eye zones and a lower tooth rectangle — the face as a set of framed compartments on a hot, high-contrast ground.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #170

stops.whyHere: Stacked rectangular panels and mismatched spiral eyes echo the compartment logic of the previous work, but the hot red field gives way to a cooler olive green.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works divide the face into hard rectangular zones; where the first burns with red and black, this one settles into olive and yellow, shifting temperature without changing structure.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #171

stops.whyHere: Nested rectangular outlines layer around a dark brown core; spiraling eye loops and a bared tooth row push the compartment system toward confrontation against a high-contrast orange field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The contained panels now multiply outward as stacked nested frames, and the orange field raises contrast sharply against the preceding work's muted olive ground.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #168

chapters.title: The Segmented Figure
chapters.introduction: Structure moves from face to full body, with plated torsos and blocky heads that treat the whole figure as an assembly of interlocking parts.

stops.whyHere: A standing figure whose wide rectangular head and striped torso are held together by two independent wandering line systems — structure and loose energy sharing the same frame.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: From a face built of nested frames, the view pulls back to a full standing figure; the rectangular head carries the same compartment logic into a body with arms and feet.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #16

stops.whyHere: A plated, gold-toned figure stands square-on, its torso divided into hard-edged panels with white zigzag marks and deep shadow at the joints — the most solidly bounded body in the gallery.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous figure is held together by wandering lines; here dense gold plating and shadow-filled joints replace that looseness, making the body feel heavily bounded rather than sketched.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #131

stops.whyHere: A squat figure crouches low, its warm amber bulk pressing toward the viewer; cyan-rimmed rectangular eye forms and a raised hand introduce unresolved tension into the plated body type.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous figure stands upright and monumental; this one crouches and crowds the frame, its looser scribbled edges and raised hand breaking the armoured stillness.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #203

chapters.title: Heads Under Pressure
chapters.introduction: These works keep the face frontal and close-cropped but surround or cross it with lines that refuse to stay behind the figure, making containment feel uncertain.

stops.whyHere: A cat-eared head on a saturated blue field, its face divided into zigzag bands and an orange inset box, with red strokes pushing outward against the blue containment.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Moving from a full crouching figure to a cropped head, the blue field holds the face firmly while jagged marks and outward-pushing strokes reintroduce the pressure of escaping energy.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #244

stops.whyHere: A black-ground face built from hard rectangular blocks — mismatched eyes, wide jaw — crossed by arcing lines in magenta, sky blue, and red that refuse to stay behind the figure.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's lines push outward from the edges; here they cross directly over the face, making the rectangular structure feel besieged rather than simply framed.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #185

stops.whyHere: A frontal face accumulated from amber and rust lines over a flat tan ground; pale scribbled eye boxes and a white tooth grid give it a fixed, wide-open quality built up layer by layer.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's crossing lines are energetic and multicoloured; here a warmer, denser accumulation of amber lines replaces that, the face built up rather than crossed.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #288

stops.whyHere: A large rounded form built from overlapping yellow, white, and blue lines with a dark interior; loose strokes escape at the edges and the composition splits into unequal halves.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work fills the frame with a tight frontal face; this one loosens the outline, letting strokes escape at the edges and splitting the composition into an uneven left and right.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #153

chapters.title: Faces as Display Boards
chapters.introduction: These works replace expected facial anatomy with panels, grids, and emblems that invite scanning rather than recognition — the head as something to be read across rather than met.

stops.whyHere: Four framed panels replace facial features, each running its own small system of loops, crosses, and zigzags — the face as a display board to be scanned rather than met.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's loose overlapping lines give way to a strictly organised face where each zone is a self-contained panel, shifting from accumulated marks to separated compartments.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #245

stops.whyHere: A diamond-shaped head under a wide-brimmed hat; yellow outlines divide the face into looping eye sockets and a barred mouth zone set against soft pooling colour fields.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's four panels are symmetrically arranged; here a diamond head and off-centre hat tilt the geometry, introducing asymmetry and ceremony into the display-board format.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #292

stops.whyHere: Large pink glasses divide a rounded turquoise head into two bright panels; a toothy emblem and yellow crown bars offer immediate recognition followed by a slower, more exploratory look.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's compartments are built from multiple yellow-outlined zones; here the system reduces to a single bold horizontal division — the glasses — against a clean turquoise ground.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #299

stops.whyHere: A gold mass pressed close to the frame edge, with a dark open cavity and scattered teal loops — no rectangular panels, held together by compressed warm colour rather than drawn compartments.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The previous work's clean turquoise and pink panels give way to a dense, pressurised gold form with no clear compartments, offering a deliberate contrast to the display-board logic preceding it.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #167

chapters.title: Scaffolding and What It Leaves Open
chapters.introduction: A single work closes the gallery: a rounded head where heavy black outlines hold colour patches in place but leave a hollow eye socket and an open hatched mouth that the structure cannot close.

stops.whyHere: A rounded head on a grey ground, its black scaffolding holding colour patches in place while a hollow eye socket and a wide hatched lower gap remain visibly unresolved — structure that does not fully close.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the previous chapter's works replaced anatomy with readable panels, this head keeps recognisable skull anatomy but leaves its most prominent features — eye and mouth — as open cavities that the black outlines frame without filling.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #166
